hook.description: Cold open on an overhead shot of a stop-motion couple in bed at night, phone-lit; the wife immediately states the accusation, 'You never flirt with me anymore,' with no preamble.
hook.why_it_works: Opens mid-argument with a relatable, universal grievance and zero setup dialogue, so the viewer is oriented in under 2 seconds and primed to want the husband's defense.

setup.description: The husband (deadpan, stone-faced, arms crossed over the blanket) offers his defense: 'I literally forwarded you a meme at 2 AM,' shown via a close-up on his unimpressed, half-lidded expression while the wife keeps scrolling her phone.

conflict.description: Implied beat rather than spoken dialogue: the silent pause after his 'meme at 2 AM' line, held on his frozen expression, lets the absurdity/inadequacy of his 'romantic gesture' land before she shuts it down.

punchline.description: The wife delivers the dismissive one-line punchline, 'Grow up,' rejecting the meme-as-romance defense outright.

ending.description: No further dialogue; the camera holds on the husband's static, defeated deadpan face (top-down close-up) for several seconds as the beat settles, then the title card 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / Created by NIN.' fades in directly over his frozen expression to close the reel.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.

beat_map.description: Wife, lit by phone glow in bed, states the accusation: 'You never flirt with me anymore.'
Husband's deadpan close-up as he defends himself: 'I literally forwarded you a meme at 2 AM.'
Held silent pause on husband's frozen expression after his weak defense, letting the tension/absurdity sit before her comeback.
Extended hold on the husband's blank, defeated face; title card 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / Created by NIN.' fades in over his face to close the reel.

narrative_notes: This is an extremely compressed 11-second reel (shorter than the typical 20-25s target), so the arc is fused: there is no separate visual 'setup' scene establishing normal life before the conflict -- the hook and setup are essentially the same held shot/exchange, with the wife's opening accusation doubling as both hook and inciting conflict statement. The 'conflict' beat here is not a new plot development but a beat of silence/held reaction on the husband's face between his line and her comeback -- there is no escalation, just a two-line volley (accusation -> weak defense -> dismissal). The punchline is a single dry line ('Grow up') rather than a visual gag or reveal. The ending is unusually long relative to total runtime (about 4 of 11 seconds, over a third of the video) because it holds on the husband's static face while the title card fades in, functioning as both the emotional 'beat' (his defeat) and the branding/credits moment simultaneously.
